source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact original XML verse substrings including written/read and other notes; no normalized reconstruction.
source.public_versification_note: Selected public verse labels match the pinned records. Complete original records, including annotations, are hashed.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial choices are independent of overlap scores. No minimum-change quota. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Keeps third-year dating without harmonizing chronology.
verses.before: In the third year of the reign of Jehoiakim king of Judah, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came to Jerusalem and besieged it.
verses.after: In the third year of Jehoiakim king of Judah’s reign, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came to Jerusalem and besieged it.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the third year of the reign of Jehoiakim king of Judah, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came to Jerusalem and besieged it.

verses.rationale: Preserves Lord title, partial vessels and repeated god's house.
verses.before: The Lord gave Jehoiakim king of Judah into his hand, along with some of the vessels of the house of God. He brought them to the land of Shinar, to the house of his god, and he brought the vessels into the treasury of his god.
verses.after: The Lord gave Jehoiakim king of Judah into his hand, along with some of the vessels from God’s house. He brought them to Shinar, to the house of his god, and placed the vessels in his god’s treasury.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Lord gave Jehoiakim king of Judah into his hand, along with some of the vessels of the house of God. He brought them to the land of Shinar, to the house of his god, and he brought the vessels into the treasury of his god.

verses.rationale: Retains eunuch designation with court-title note.
verses.before: Then the king said to Ashpenaz, chief of his eunuchs, to bring some from the children of Israel, from the royal offspring and from the nobles,
verses.after: The king ordered Ashpenaz, chief of his eunuchs, to bring in some Israelites from the royal family and the nobility:
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the king said to Ashpenaz, chief of his eunuchs, to bring some from the children of Israel, from the royal offspring and from the nobles,

verses.rationale: Keeps male selection and full qualifications.
verses.before: young men without any defect, good in appearance, discerning in all wisdom, knowing knowledge, understanding learning, and capable of standing in the king’s palace, and to teach them the literature and language of the Chaldeans.
verses.after: young men without any physical defect, handsome, skilled in every kind of wisdom, knowledgeable, discerning, and capable of serving in the king’s palace. They were to be taught the literature and language of the Chaldeans.
verses.tsw_comparator: young men without any defect, good in appearance, discerning in all wisdom, knowing knowledge, understanding learning, and capable of standing in the king’s palace, and to teach them the literature and language of the Chaldeans.

verses.rationale: Preserves daily allotment and three-year period.
verses.before: The king appointed for them a daily portion from the king’s delicacies and from the wine that he drank. They were to be educated for three years, and at the end of them they were to stand before the king.
verses.after: The king assigned them a daily portion of his own food and the wine he drank. They were to be trained for three years, then enter the king’s service.
verses.tsw_comparator: The king appointed for them a daily portion from the king’s delicacies and from the wine that he drank. They were to be educated for three years, and at the end of them they were to stand before the king.

verses.rationale: Keeps four Hebrew names and origin.
verses.before: Among them were some from the children of Judah: Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah.
verses.after: Among them were Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah, from Judah.
verses.tsw_comparator: Among them were some from the children of Judah: Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah.

verses.rationale: Preserves each exact name pairing.
verses.before: The chief of the eunuchs gave them names: he gave Daniel the name Belteshazzar, Hananiah the name Shadrach, Mishael the name Meshach, and Azariah the name Abednego.
verses.after: The chief eunuch gave them new names: Daniel he called Belteshazzar; Hananiah, Shadrach; Mishael, Meshach; and Azariah, Abed-nego.
verses.tsw_comparator: The chief of the eunuchs gave them names: he gave Daniel the name Belteshazzar, Hananiah the name Shadrach, Mishael the name Meshach, and Azariah the name Abednego.

verses.rationale: Keeps defilement repeated without inventing motive.
verses.before: Yet Daniel set it upon his heart that he would not defile himself with the king’s delicacies or with the wine that he drank. So he sought permission from the chief of the eunuchs not to defile himself.
verses.after: Daniel resolved not to defile himself with the king’s food or the wine he drank. He asked the chief eunuch for permission to avoid defiling himself.
verses.tsw_comparator: But Daniel set it upon his heart that he would not defile himself with the king’s delicacies or with the wine that he drank. So he sought permission from the chief of the eunuchs not to defile himself.

verses.rationale: Preserves divine cause and paired favor terms.
verses.before: God gave Daniel steadfast kindness and compassion before the chief of the eunuchs.
verses.after: God caused the chief eunuch to show Daniel kindness and compassion.
verses.tsw_comparator: God gave Daniel steadfast kindness and compassion before the chief of the eunuchs.

verses.rationale: Keeps personal danger and comparative concern.
verses.before: But the chief of the eunuchs said to Daniel, “I fear my lord the king, who appointed your food and your drink. Why should he see your faces looking worse than the young men your own age? Then you would make my head guilty before the king.”
verses.after: But the chief eunuch told Daniel, “I am afraid of my lord the king, who assigned your food and drink. Why should he see you looking worse than the other young men your age? You would put my head at risk with the king.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But the chief of the eunuchs said to Daniel, “I fear my lord the king, who appointed your food and your drink. Why should he see your faces looking worse than the young men your own age? Then you would make my head guilty before the king.”

verses.rationale: Distinguishes steward from chief and repeats names.
verses.before: Then Daniel said to the steward whom the chief of the eunuchs had appointed over Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah,
verses.after: Daniel then spoke to the steward whom the chief eunuch had appointed over Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah:
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Daniel said to the steward whom the chief of the eunuchs had appointed over Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah,

verses.rationale: Keeps ten days and request, not dietary prescription.
verses.before: “Please test your servants for ten days. Let vegetables be given to us to eat and water to drink.
verses.after: “Please test your servants for ten days. Give us vegetables to eat and water to drink.
verses.tsw_comparator: “Please test your servants for ten days. Let vegetables be given to us to eat and water to drink.

verses.rationale: Preserves requested empirical comparison and discretion.
verses.before: Then let our appearance and the appearance of the young men who eat the king’s delicacies be seen before you, and deal with your servants according to what you see.”
verses.after: Then compare our appearance with that of the young men eating the king’s food. Deal with your servants according to what you see.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then let our appearance and the appearance of the young men who eat the king’s delicacies be seen before you, and deal with your servants according to what you see.”

verses.rationale: Retains explicit duration repetition.
verses.before: So he listened to them in this matter and tested them for ten days.
verses.after: He agreed and tested them for ten days.
verses.tsw_comparator: So he listened to them in this matter and tested them for ten days.

verses.rationale: Keeps fuller flesh rather than modern thinness ideal.
verses.before: At the end of ten days their appearance was better and their flesh fuller than all the young men who ate the king’s delicacies.
verses.after: At the end of ten days, they looked better and fuller in body than all the young men eating the king’s food.
verses.tsw_comparator: At the end of ten days their appearance was better and their flesh fuller than all the young men who ate the king’s delicacies.

verses.rationale: Preserves ongoing substitution without inventing disposal.
verses.before: So the steward continued taking away their delicacies and the wine they were to drink and gave them vegetables.
verses.after: So the steward continued taking away their assigned food and wine and giving them vegetables.
verses.tsw_comparator: So the steward continued taking away their delicacies and the wine they were to drink and gave them vegetables.

verses.rationale: Distinguishes shared gifts from Daniel's additional understanding.
verses.before: As for these four young men, God gave them knowledge and skill in every kind of literature and wisdom, and Daniel had understanding in every kind of vision and dream.
verses.after: God gave all four of these young men knowledge and insight into every kind of literature and wisdom. Daniel also understood visions and dreams of every kind.
verses.tsw_comparator: As for these four young men, God gave them knowledge and skill in every kind of literature and wisdom, and Daniel had understanding in every kind of vision and dream.

verses.rationale: Keeps appointed training endpoint.
verses.before: At the end of the days when the king had said they should be brought in, the chief of the eunuchs brought them in before Nebuchadnezzar.
verses.after: When the time set by the king for bringing them in had ended, the chief eunuch presented them to Nebuchadnezzar.
verses.tsw_comparator: At the end of the days when the king had said they should be brought in, the chief of the eunuchs brought them in before Nebuchadnezzar.

verses.rationale: Preserves four names and outcome.
verses.before: The king spoke with them, and among them all none was found like Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah. So they stood before the king.
verses.after: The king spoke with them. Among them all, no one matched Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah, so they entered the king’s service.
verses.tsw_comparator: The king spoke with them, and among them all none was found like Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah. So they stood before the king.

verses.rationale: Keeps tenfold comparison and both specialist groups.
verses.before: In every matter of wisdom and understanding about which the king questioned them, he found them ten times better than all the magicians and enchanters who were in all his kingdom.
verses.after: In every matter of wisdom and understanding he asked about, the king found them ten times better than all the magicians and enchanters in his entire kingdom.
verses.tsw_comparator: In every matter of wisdom and understanding about which the king questioned them, he found them ten times better than all the magicians and enchanters who were in all his kingdom.

verses.rationale: Does not imply death at the stated endpoint.
verses.before: Daniel remained until the first year of King Cyrus.
verses.after: Daniel remained until the first year of King Cyrus.
verses.tsw_comparator: And Daniel remained until the first year of King Cyrus.

verses.rationale: Keeps repeated name and difficult sleeplessness idiom.
verses.before: In the second year of Nebuchadnezzar’s reign, Nebuchadnezzar dreamed dreams, and his spirit was troubled, and his sleep left him.
verses.after: In the second year of Nebuchadnezzar’s reign, Nebuchadnezzar had dreams. His spirit was troubled, and his sleep left him.
verses.tsw_comparator: In the second year of Nebuchadnezzar’s reign, Nebuchadnezzar dreamed dreams, and his spirit was troubled, and his sleep left him.

verses.rationale: Preserves four distinct court groups.
verses.before: Then the king commanded that the magicians, enchanters, sorcerers, and Chaldeans be called to tell the king his dreams. So they came and stood before the king.
verses.after: The king ordered the magicians, enchanters, sorcerers, and Chaldeans summoned to tell him his dreams. They came and stood before the king.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the king commanded that the magicians, enchanters, sorcerers, and Chaldeans be called to tell the king his dreams. So they came and stood before the king.

verses.rationale: Keeps troubled spirit and knowing dream.
verses.before: The king said to them, “I have dreamed a dream, and my spirit is troubled to know the dream.”
verses.after: The king told them, “I have had a dream, and my spirit is troubled. I want to understand the dream.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The king said to them, “I have dreamed a dream, and my spirit is troubled to know the dream.”

verses.rationale: Retains language marker and singular read-form servant.
verses.before: Then the Chaldeans spoke to the king in Aramaic: “O king, live forever! Tell the dream to your servants, and we will declare the interpretation.”
verses.after: The Chaldeans answered the king in Aramaic, “May the king live forever! Tell your servant the dream, and we will explain its meaning.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the Chaldeans spoke to the king in Aramaic: “O king, live forever! Tell the dream to your servants, and we will declare the interpretation.”

verses.rationale: Keeps decision reading and explicit bodily threat.
verses.before: The king answered and said to the Chaldeans, “The word from me is firm: if you do not reveal to me the dream and its interpretation, you will be torn limb from limb, and your houses will be made a refuse heap.
verses.after: The king replied to the Chaldeans, “My decision is firm. If you do not tell me the dream and its meaning, you will be torn limb from limb and your houses reduced to refuse heaps.
verses.tsw_comparator: The king answered and said to the Chaldeans, “The word from me is firm: if you do not make known to me the dream and its interpretation, you shall be torn limb from limb, and your houses shall be made a refuse heap.

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated paired demand and three rewards.
verses.before: But if you declare the dream and its interpretation, you will receive from me gifts, reward, and great honor. Therefore declare to me the dream and its interpretation.”
verses.after: But if you tell me the dream and its meaning, you will receive gifts, rewards, and great honor from me. So tell me the dream and its meaning.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But if you declare the dream and its interpretation, you shall receive from me gifts, reward, and great honor. Therefore declare to me the dream and its interpretation.”

verses.rationale: Keeps second request and plural servants.
verses.before: They answered a second time and said, “Let the king tell the dream to his servants, and we will declare its interpretation.”
verses.after: They answered again, “Let the king tell his servants the dream, and we will explain its meaning.”
verses.tsw_comparator: They answered a second time and said, “Let the king tell the dream to his servants, and we will declare its interpretation.”

verses.rationale: Retains buying-time idiom and repeated firmness.
verses.before: The king answered and said, “I know for certain that you are buying time because you see that the word from me is firm.
verses.after: The king replied, “I know for certain that you are buying time, because you see that my decision is firm.
verses.tsw_comparator: The king answered and said, “I know for certain that you are buying time because you see that the word from me is firm.

verses.rationale: Keeps test of interpretation and alleged collusion.
verses.before: If you do not reveal to me the dream, there is one decree for you. You have agreed to speak lying and corrupt words before me until the time changes. Therefore tell me the dream, and I will know that you can declare its interpretation to me.”
verses.after: If you do not tell me the dream, there is only one sentence for you. You have agreed to tell me lying, corrupt words until the situation changes. So tell me the dream, and I will know you can explain its meaning.”
verses.tsw_comparator: If you do not make known to me the dream, there is one decree for you. You have agreed to speak lying and corrupt words before me until the time changes. Therefore tell me the dream, and I will know that you can declare its interpretation to me.”

verses.rationale: Preserves universal impossibility claim and specialist list.
verses.before: The Chaldeans answered before the king and said, “There is no person upon the earth who can declare the king’s matter. Therefore no great and powerful king has asked such a thing from any magician, enchanter, or Chaldean.
verses.after: The Chaldeans answered the king, “No one on earth can do what the king asks. No king, however great and powerful, has ever asked such a thing of any magician, enchanter, or Chaldean.
verses.tsw_comparator: The Chaldeans answered before the king and said, “There is no person upon the earth who can declare the king’s matter. Therefore no great and powerful king has asked such a thing from any magician, enchanter, or Chaldean.

verses.rationale: Keeps divine/human dwelling contrast without endorsing speakers.
verses.before: The matter that the king asks is difficult, and there is no other who can declare it before the king except the gods, whose dwelling is not with flesh.”
verses.after: What the king asks is difficult. No one can reveal it to the king except the gods, who do not dwell with flesh.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The matter that the king asks is difficult, and there is no other who can declare it before the king except the gods, whose dwelling is not with flesh.”

verses.rationale: Retains indiscriminate lethal command.
verses.before: Because of this the king became angry and very furious and commanded that all the wise men of Babylon be destroyed.
verses.after: At this the king became furious and ordered all Babylon’s wise men destroyed.
verses.tsw_comparator: Because of this the king became angry and very furious and commanded that all the wise men of Babylon be destroyed.

verses.rationale: Preserves participial execution language with timing note.
verses.before: So the decree went out that the wise men were to be killed, and they sought Daniel and his companions to kill them.
verses.after: The decree went out, and the wise men were being put to death. They also sought Daniel and his companions to kill them.
verses.tsw_comparator: So the decree went out that the wise men were to be killed, and they sought Daniel and his companions to kill them.

verses.rationale: Keeps executioner's actual function and Daniel's manner.
verses.before: Then Daniel responded with counsel and discretion to Arioch, captain of the king’s guard, who had gone out to kill the wise men of Babylon.
verses.after: Then Daniel responded with counsel and tact to Arioch, the king’s chief executioner, who had gone out to kill Babylon’s wise men.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Daniel responded with counsel and discretion to Arioch, captain of the king’s guard, who had gone out to kill the wise men of Babylon.

verses.rationale: Uses harsh with urgent alternative noted.
verses.before: He answered and said to Arioch, the king’s officer, “Why is the decree from the king so severe?” Then Arioch made the matter known to Daniel.
verses.after: He asked Arioch, the king’s officer, “Why is the king’s decree so harsh?” Arioch explained the matter to Daniel.
verses.tsw_comparator: He answered and said to Arioch, the king’s officer, “Why is the decree from the king so severe?” Then Arioch made the matter known to Daniel.

verses.rationale: Keeps requested time despite accusation of delay.
verses.before: Daniel went in and asked the king to give him time, so that he might declare the interpretation to the king.
verses.after: Daniel went in and asked the king to give him time, so he could explain the dream’s meaning to the king.
verses.tsw_comparator: Daniel went in and asked the king to give him time, so that he might declare the interpretation to the king.

verses.rationale: Retains Hebrew names in private setting.
verses.before: Then Daniel went to his house and made the matter known to Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah, his companions,
verses.after: Then Daniel went home and explained the matter to his companions Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Daniel went to his house and made the matter known to Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah, his companions,

verses.rationale: Keeps mercy and shared peril.
verses.before: so that they might seek mercies from the God of heaven concerning this mystery, so that Daniel and his companions would not be destroyed with the rest of the wise men of Babylon.
verses.after: He urged them to ask the God of heaven for mercy concerning this mystery, so Daniel and his companions would not perish with the rest of Babylon’s wise men.
verses.tsw_comparator: so that they might seek mercies from the God of heaven concerning this mystery, so that Daniel and his companions would not be destroyed with the rest of the wise men of Babylon.

verses.rationale: Preserves night vision rather than recasting as dream.
verses.before: Then the mystery was revealed to Daniel in a vision of the night. Then Daniel blessed the God of heaven.
verses.after: During the night the mystery was revealed to Daniel in a vision. Then Daniel blessed the God of heaven.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the mystery was revealed to Daniel in a vision of the night. Then Daniel blessed the God of heaven.

verses.rationale: Keeps poetic praise and paired divine gifts.
verses.before: Daniel answered and said: “Blessed be the name of God from age to age, for wisdom and might belong to him.
verses.after: Daniel said: “May God’s name be blessed from age to age, for wisdom and power belong to him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Daniel answered and said: “Blessed be the name of God from age to age, for wisdom and might belong to him.

verses.rationale: Retains four parallel divine actions.
verses.before: He changes times and seasons; he removes kings and raises up kings. He gives wisdom to the wise and knowledge to people who know understanding.
verses.after: He changes times and seasons; he removes kings and raises up kings. He gives wisdom to the wise and knowledge to those with understanding.
verses.tsw_comparator: He changes times and seasons; he removes kings and raises up kings. He gives wisdom to the wise and knowledge to those who know understanding.

verses.rationale: Keeps revelation and light/dark contrast.
verses.before: He reveals deep and hidden things; he knows what is in the darkness, and light dwells with him.
verses.after: He reveals deep and hidden things; he knows what is in the darkness, and light dwells with him.
verses.tsw_comparator: He reveals deep and hidden things; he knows what is in the darkness, and light dwells with him.

verses.rationale: Preserves me/we/us shifts and repeated knowing.
verses.before: To you, God of my ancestors, I give thanks and praise, for you have given me wisdom and might. And now you have revealed to me what we asked of you, for you have revealed to us the king’s matter.”
verses.after: God of my ancestors, I thank and praise you. You have given me wisdom and power; now you have made known to me what we asked of you. You have made the king’s matter known to us.”
verses.tsw_comparator: To you, God of my ancestors, I give thanks and praise, for you have given me wisdom and might. And now you have made known to me what we asked of you, for you have made known to us the king’s matter.”

verses.rationale: Keeps rescue extending beyond Daniel's companions.
verses.before: So Daniel went in to Arioch, whom the king had appointed to destroy the wise men of Babylon. He went and said thus to him: “Do not destroy the wise men of Babylon. Bring me in before the king, and I will declare the interpretation to the king.”
verses.after: So Daniel went to Arioch, whom the king had appointed to destroy Babylon’s wise men. He told him, “Do not destroy Babylon’s wise men. Bring me before the king, and I will explain the meaning to him.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore Daniel went in to Arioch, whom the king had appointed to destroy the wise men of Babylon. He went and said thus to him: “Do not destroy the wise men of Babylon. Bring me in before the king, and I will declare the interpretation to the king.”

verses.rationale: Preserves Arioch's claim as his own speech.
verses.before: Then Arioch hurriedly brought Daniel in before the king and said thus to him: “I have found a man from the exiles of Judah who will make the interpretation known to the king.”
verses.after: Arioch hurried Daniel before the king and said, “I have found a man among the exiles from Judah who can explain the meaning to the king.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Arioch hurriedly brought Daniel in before the king and said thus to him: “I have found a man from the exiles of Judah who will make the interpretation known to the king.”

verses.rationale: Keeps both names and paired question.
verses.before: The king answered and said to Daniel, whose name was Belteshazzar, “Are you able to reveal to me the dream that I saw and its interpretation?”
verses.after: The king asked Daniel, whose name was Belteshazzar, “Can you tell me the dream I saw and its meaning?”
verses.tsw_comparator: The king answered and said to Daniel, whose name was Belteshazzar, “Are you able to make known to me the dream that I saw and its interpretation?”

verses.rationale: Preserves four groups' inability.
verses.before: Daniel answered before the king and said, “The mystery that the king asks, no wise men, enchanters, magicians, or diviners can declare to the king.
verses.after: Daniel answered the king, “No wise men, enchanters, magicians, or diviners can reveal to the king the mystery he asks about.
verses.tsw_comparator: Daniel answered before the king and said, “The mystery that the king asks, no wise men, enchanters, magicians, or diviners can declare to the king.

verses.rationale: Keeps revelation source and future language without date scheme.
verses.before: But there is a God in the heavens who reveals mysteries, and he has revealed to King Nebuchadnezzar what will be in the latter days. Your dream and the visions of your head upon your bed were these:
verses.after: But there is a God in heaven who reveals mysteries. He has shown King Nebuchadnezzar what will happen in days to come. This was your dream, the visions that passed through your mind as you lay in bed:
verses.tsw_comparator: But there is a God in the heavens who reveals mysteries, and he has made known to King Nebuchadnezzar what will be in the latter days. Your dream and the visions of your head upon your bed were these:

verses.rationale: Retains repeated future revelation.
verses.before: “As for you, O king, your thoughts upon your bed turned to what would be after this, and the revealer of mysteries revealed to you what will be.
verses.after: As you lay in bed, O king, thoughts came to you about what would happen afterward. The revealer of mysteries has shown you what will happen.
verses.tsw_comparator: “As for you, O king, your thoughts upon your bed turned to what would be after this, and the revealer of mysteries made known to you what will be.

verses.rationale: Preserves denial of personal superiority and revelatory purpose.
verses.before: But as for me, this mystery was not revealed to me because of wisdom that is in me more than in any living person, but so that the interpretation may be revealed to the king and that you may know the thoughts of your heart.
verses.after: This mystery was revealed to me because the king was to be told its meaning and understand the thoughts of his heart, not because I have more wisdom than anyone else alive.
verses.tsw_comparator: But as for me, this mystery was not revealed to me because of wisdom that is in me more than in any living person, but so that the interpretation may be made known to the king and that you may know the thoughts of your heart.

verses.rationale: Keeps size, brilliance and terror distinct.
verses.before: You, O king, were looking, and look, there was one great statue. This statue was enormous, and its brightness was extraordinary. It stood before you, and its appearance was terrifying.
verses.after: “You looked, O king, and there stood a great statue. This immense statue was dazzling, standing before you, terrifying to behold.
verses.tsw_comparator: You, O king, were looking, and look, there was one great statue. This statue was enormous, and its brightness was extraordinary. It stood before you, and its appearance was terrifying.

verses.rationale: Preserves body-to-metal sequence.
verses.before: The head of that statue was of fine gold, its chest and arms of silver, its belly and thighs of bronze,
verses.after: Its head was fine gold; its chest and arms were silver; its belly and thighs were bronze;
verses.tsw_comparator: The head of that statue was of fine gold, its chest and arms of silver, its belly and thighs of bronze,

verses.rationale: Keeps mixed feet after iron legs.
verses.before: its legs of iron, its feet partly of iron and partly of clay.
verses.after: its legs were iron, and its feet partly iron and partly clay.
verses.tsw_comparator: its legs of iron, its feet partly of iron and partly of clay.

verses.rationale: Retains unmentioned cutting agent and point of impact.
verses.before: You were looking until a stone was cut out, not by hands, and it struck the statue on its feet of iron and clay and shattered them.
verses.after: As you watched, a stone was cut out without hands. It struck the statue on its iron-and-clay feet and crushed them.
verses.tsw_comparator: You were looking until a stone was cut out, not by hands, and it struck the statue on its feet of iron and clay and shattered them.

verses.rationale: Preserves full material list and agricultural simile.
verses.before: Then the iron, clay, bronze, silver, and gold were shattered together and became like chaff from the summer threshing floors. The wind carried them away so that no trace of them was found. But the stone that struck the statue became a great mountain and filled the entire earth.
verses.after: Then the iron, clay, bronze, silver, and gold were crushed together and became like chaff on summer threshing floors. The wind carried them away, leaving no trace. But the stone that struck the statue became a great mountain and filled the whole earth.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the iron, clay, bronze, silver, and gold were shattered together and became like chaff from the summer threshing floors. The wind carried them away so that no trace of them was found. But the stone that struck the statue became a great mountain and filled the whole earth.

verses.rationale: Retains plural we without inventing co-speakers.
verses.before: “This was the dream. Now we will tell its interpretation before the king.
verses.after: “That was the dream. Now we will tell the king its meaning.
verses.tsw_comparator: “This was the dream. Now we will tell its interpretation before the king.

verses.rationale: Keeps four gifts and source of kingship.
verses.before: You, O king, king of kings, to whom the God of heaven has given the kingdom, power, strength, and glory,
verses.after: You, O king, are king of kings. The God of heaven has given you the kingdom, power, strength, and honor.
verses.tsw_comparator: You, O king, king of kings, to whom the God of heaven has given the kingdom, power, strength, and glory,

verses.rationale: Preserves nonhuman dominion and explicit sole identification.
verses.before: and into whose hand he has given wherever the children of humanity dwell, the animals of the field, and the birds of the heavens, and has made you ruler over them all—you are the head of gold.
verses.after: Wherever human beings live, he has given them into your hand, along with the beasts of the field and birds of the sky, making you ruler over them all. You are the head of gold.
verses.tsw_comparator: and into whose hand he has given wherever the children of humanity dwell, the animals of the field, and the birds of the heavens, and has made you ruler over them all—you are the head of gold.

verses.rationale: Keeps kingdoms unnamed and ordinal sequence.
verses.before: After you another kingdom will arise, inferior to you, and another third kingdom of bronze, which will rule over all the earth.
verses.after: After you another kingdom will arise, inferior to yours. Then a third kingdom, of bronze, will rule the whole earth.
verses.tsw_comparator: After you another kingdom will arise, inferior to you, and another third kingdom of bronze, which will rule over all the earth.

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated destructive iron comparison.
verses.before: Then there will be a fourth kingdom, strong as iron, because iron crushes and shatters everything. Like iron that breaks all these, it will crush and break.
verses.after: A fourth kingdom will be strong as iron. As iron crushes and shatters everything, and like iron that breaks all these things, it will crush and break them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then there will be a fourth kingdom, strong as iron, because iron crushes and shatters everything. Like iron that breaks all these, it will crush and break.

verses.rationale: Keeps divided composition and residual strength.
verses.before: And as you saw the feet and toes partly of potter’s clay and partly of iron, it will be a divided kingdom, but some of the strength of iron will be in it, just as you saw iron mixed with soft clay.
verses.after: You saw feet and toes partly of potter’s clay and partly of iron. The kingdom will be divided, yet some of iron’s strength will remain in it, just as you saw iron mixed with clay.
verses.tsw_comparator: And as you saw the feet and toes partly of potter’s clay and partly of iron, it will be a divided kingdom, but some of the strength of iron will be in it, just as you saw iron mixed with soft clay.

verses.rationale: Preserves proportion without inventing number of rulers.
verses.before: And as the toes of the feet were partly iron and partly clay, so the kingdom will be partly strong and partly brittle.
verses.after: As the toes were partly iron and partly clay, the kingdom will be partly strong and partly brittle.
verses.tsw_comparator: And as the toes of the feet were partly iron and partly clay, so the kingdom will be partly strong and partly brittle.

verses.rationale: Keeps seed-of-humans phrase with marriage alternative noted.
verses.before: As you saw iron mixed with soft clay, they will mix with the offspring of humanity, but they will not cling to one another, just as iron does not mix with clay.
verses.after: As you saw iron mixed with clay, they will mingle through human offspring, but they will not hold together, just as iron does not mix with clay.
verses.tsw_comparator: As you saw iron mixed with soft clay, they will mix with the offspring of humanity, but they will not cling to one another, just as iron does not mix with clay.

verses.rationale: Preserves permanence and destructive replacement.
verses.before: “And in the days of those kings, the God of heaven will establish a kingdom that will never be destroyed, and that kingdom will not be left to another people. It will crush and bring all these kingdoms to an end, and it will stand forever,
verses.after: In the days of those kings, the God of heaven will establish a kingdom that will never be destroyed or handed over to another people. It will crush all these kingdoms and bring them to an end, but it will stand forever.
verses.tsw_comparator: “And in the days of those kings, the God of heaven will establish a kingdom that will never be destroyed, and that kingdom will not be left to another people. It will crush and bring all these kingdoms to an end, and it will stand forever,

verses.rationale: Keeps mountain detail and changed material-list order.
verses.before: just as you saw that a stone was cut from the mountain, not by hands, and that it shattered the iron, bronze, clay, silver, and gold. The great God has revealed to the king what will happen after this. The dream is certain, and its interpretation is trustworthy.”
verses.after: That is why you saw a stone cut from the mountain without hands, crushing iron, bronze, clay, silver, and gold. The great God has shown the king what will happen afterward. The dream is certain, and its meaning is trustworthy.”
verses.tsw_comparator: just as you saw that a stone was cut from the mountain, not by hands, and that it shattered the iron, bronze, clay, silver, and gold. The great God has made known to the king what will happen after this. The dream is certain, and its interpretation is trustworthy.”

verses.rationale: Preserves honor directed at Daniel without invented refusal.
verses.before: Then King Nebuchadnezzar fell upon his face, bowed down before Daniel, and commanded that an offering and incense be presented to him.
verses.after: Then King Nebuchadnezzar fell facedown and bowed before Daniel. He ordered an offering and incense presented to him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then King Nebuchadnezzar fell upon his face, bowed down before Daniel, and commanded that an offering and incense be presented to him.

verses.rationale: Keeps king's confession and plural your.
verses.before: The king answered Daniel and said, “Truly your God is God of gods and Lord of kings and a revealer of mysteries, since you could reveal this mystery.”
verses.after: The king told Daniel, “Truly, your God is God of gods and Lord of kings, a revealer of mysteries, since you could reveal this mystery.”
verses.tsw_comparator: The king answered Daniel and said, “Truly your God is God of gods and Lord of kings and a revealer of mysteries, since you were able to reveal this mystery.”

verses.rationale: Preserves four acts of promotion.
verses.before: Then the king made Daniel great and gave him many great gifts and made him ruler over the whole province of Babylon and chief prefect over all the wise men of Babylon.
verses.after: Then the king promoted Daniel, gave him many great gifts, made him ruler over the whole province of Babylon, and appointed him chief over all Babylon’s wise men.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the king made Daniel great and gave him many great gifts and made him ruler over the whole province of Babylon and chief prefect over all the wise men of Babylon.

verses.rationale: Keeps companions' appointments distinct from Daniel's location.
verses.before: Daniel made a request of the king, and he appointed Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego over the administration of the province of Babylon, while Daniel remained at the king’s court.
verses.after: At Daniel’s request the king appointed Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego over the affairs of Babylon’s province. Daniel remained at the king’s court.
verses.tsw_comparator: Daniel made a request of the king, and he appointed Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego over the administration of the province of Babylon, while Daniel remained at the king’s court.

comparative_references.scope: All 70 TSW verses bound and compared programmatically after independent drafting from each selected original-language record and all annotations. Selected differences read during focused authoring checks. Overlap is triage only.
